name: hojo
style: Hand-drawn 1980s-1990s Japanese cel animation in the style of Tsukasa Hojo (City Hunter, Cat's Eye). Crisp ink line art, flat cel shading, warm dusty 35mm film grain, painted background art with visible brushwork, retro urban realism. Absolutely no 3D render, no CGI, no plastic skin, no airbrushed glossy finish.
character: an adult East Asian woman in her late twenties, confident and self-possessed, sleek short straight hair with a strong purple tint, off-shoulder knit top, elegant and a little seductive but always composed. She has a private silly streak: unfinished selfies, getting tangled in cables, a pole jammed in a doorway, an out-of-focus grimace at a screen.
layout: Extreme long shot, wide establishing composition. The woman and everything she touches sit in the bottom-right corner and take up only 15% of the frame. The left, top and centre 85% stay open and uncluttered, showing the view through the window and the reflective floor, so desktop icons have somewhere to live. Nothing may cross the open area.
motion: Locked-off camera, one continuous take, no cuts, and the last frame lands back on the first so the loop has no seam. Only the smallest motion, the kind you notice a second late: she breathes, blinks, and her weight settles by a hair; a few strands of her hair and the loose knit of her top drift in the slowest breeze; outside, water crawls down the glass and the light eases a shade. No action of any kind: she does not stand, turn, cross or uncross her legs, lift, reach for or pick anything up, and nothing on the desk moves from where it is. One recognizable action is what makes a loop feel like a loop.

scenes.desc: a wet downtown skyline at night seen from a high floor, neon bleeding into rain on the glass, a few lit windows still on
a river city at dusk, low sun on the water, towers turning on one by one
deep green bamboo forest in fine rain, mist drifting between the stalks, water running down the glass
an ocean of cloud below the window, peaks poking through, light coming up sideways
a coastal road at dusk, a long flat horizon, waves breaking white far below
a snow valley at blue hour, bare larch slopes, one warm window lit across the way
stone steps and maple red on a hill, seen far off through the window frame, lanterns not yet lit
a dry plain burning orange at the end of the day, wind moving dust across an empty road

interactions.desc: working in the same frame, hunched over a terminal or a board, sleeves pushed up, sharing the shift with the viewer
chin on both hands, looking up from the screen toward the viewer, a mug of coffee still steaming beside her
leaning back from the desk with both arms up in a long stretch, eyes half shut, having just finished something
tilted head, staring at a wall of logs with an honest look of confusion, mouth slightly open
asleep sitting up, cheek on her own arm, one monitor still glowing, pen still in hand
fist raised in a small quiet victory, the other hand still on the keyboard

room: Kept things stand on the shelf above the desk, on the windowsill, on the wall beside the window, or lean against the wall on the floor. Nothing digital, nothing that looks bought yesterday.
note_layout: Extreme long shot for the room, but the note is a foreground object: she holds it out toward the camera at full arm length, square to the camera, so it sits large and sharp in the bottom-right of the frame, in front of her and overlapping the lower part of her. Everything left of centre and everything above her stays open and uncluttered, showing the view through the window and the reflective floor, so desktop icons have somewhere to live. Nothing else may cross the open area.

notePoses.desc: turned to us and holding a small square of paper out at full arm length, flat and square to the camera, eyes on us over the top of it
holding a small whiteboard up with both hands, its face square to the camera, a pen still in one hand
pressing a sticky note flat against the window glass beside her and leaning back out of its way, face turned to us
holding the paper up above her head at full arm length, face square to the camera, chin up

idle: alone at the window, stretching after a long day, watching the view instead of the screen
